solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Appropriate how birds returned (6)

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: as = how, as in 'do it as I say'

annotation.surface: Someone guesses at the right way birds come home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as an adjective, but it is the verb: to assume power is to appropriate it.
annotation.definitionFit: To assume a right or title is to take it for yourself, which is what appropriating means.

clue.text: Learner without instruction went to work under car (10)

indicators.note: in a down answer, what is under comes after

blocks.note: to act = to work, as a drug acts

annotation.surface: A mechanic's apprentice teaches himself by sliding under a car.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'under car' puts the car on top, so AUTO comes first.
annotation.definitionFit: An autodidact is self-taught: a learner who had no teacher.

clue.text: Tiny excerpt from Pilgrim’s Progress (5)

definitions.note: 'Tiny' is used as a noun, a tiny child

indicators.note: an excerpt is a piece lifted out of a text, so the answer sits inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A small passage quoted from Bunyan's allegory.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tiny' looks like an adjective describing the excerpt; it is a noun for a small child. Sprog is British slang for a baby or child.
annotation.definitionFit: A sprog is informal British slang for a small child, a tiny.

clue.text: Disapproves of alien attitude (7)

blocks.note: if she minds your smoking, she disapproves of it

annotation.surface: Someone frowns on the outlook of a foreigner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Alien' seems to describe the attitude; it is its own piece, the film's extra-terrestrial.
annotation.definitionFit: A mindset is a settled way of thinking, an attitude.

clue.text: What’s Oscar carried back in preserve bottle? (8)

indicators.note: going back runs the letters the other way
the reversed letters go in the preserve

blocks.note: jam = fruit preserve; it opens round the rest
O (Oscar in the NATO alphabet) + BORE (carried), turned round

annotation.surface: A question about what an Oscar winner lugged home in a jar of jam.
annotation.walkthrough: A jeroboam is an outsize wine or champagne bottle, holding several ordinary bottles' worth.
annotation.definitionFit: A jeroboam is a large bottle, usually of champagne.

clue.text: Eliminate onset of Americanisation in language (5)

indicators.note: the onset is the start, so take the first letter
that letter goes inside the language

blocks.note: Erse = Scottish or Irish Gaelic; it opens round the A

annotation.surface: A purist wants to stamp out the first signs of American usage in English.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a language purist's complaint, but the language is Erse, the Gaelic of Scotland or Ireland.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to rub out a mark is to get rid of it entirely.

clue.text: Controlled German article seized by French airport (7)

indicators.note: what is seized is held, so the article sits inside the airport

blocks.note: Orly, the Paris airport; it opens round DER

annotation.surface: A German newspaper piece is impounded at a Paris airport.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Controlled' reads as a verb in the past tense; it is the adjective, as in a controlled, orderly queue.
annotation.definitionFit: An orderly crowd is a controlled one, kept in good order.

clue.text: Fair goal (9)

blocks.note: fair in the sense unbiased, judging by the facts alone
a goal in the sense of an aim, not a score

annotation.surface: A verdict on a football score: the goal was fair.
annotation.walkthrough: The adjective and the noun happen to be spelt the same.
annotation.definitionFit: An objective judge is fair; an objective is also a goal to reach.

clue.text: Times piece introduces language of island race (4)

indicators.note: the piece comes first and introduces the times sign

blocks.note: a man is a piece in chess or draughts

annotation.surface: A newspaper article introduces the tongue of an island people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Times piece' looks like an article in this newspaper; the two words split. Manx is the Celtic language of the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea.
annotation.definitionFit: Manx is the Gaelic language of the Isle of Man's people.

clue.text: Internal lake splits dock in an odd way (8)

indicators.note: the inserted letters split the dock into two parts

blocks.note: a quay is a dock; it is split round INT L

annotation.surface: An inland lake cuts across a dockyard in some strange fashion.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is an adverbial phrase to match the -LY ending: oddly, quaintly.
annotation.definitionFit: To do something quaintly is to do it in an oddly old-fashioned, curious way.

clue.text: Creature natural at jumping (9)

indicators.note: letters that jump about land in a new order

annotation.surface: An animal born to leap.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a born jumper; it is a big hairy spider.
annotation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large hairy spider, a creature.

clue.text: City lover from Scotland surrounded by noise (5)

indicators.note: the lover sits inside the noise

blocks.note: din = noise; it opens round JO
jo is a Scots word for a sweetheart, as in Burns

annotation.surface: A Scottish sweetheart in a noisy town.
annotation.walkthrough: Dijon is a French city, known for its mustard.
annotation.definitionFit: Dijon is a city in Burgundy, eastern France.

clue.text: Food processor gives diet out by leaflet (9,5)

indicators.note: 'out' as in put out of joint: the letters are knocked out of their proper order
by = beside, so the leaflet follows

blocks.note: a tract is a leaflet, often religious

annotation.surface: A kitchen gadget comes with a diet pamphlet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Food processor' is the kitchen machine in the surface; the answer is the body's own.
annotation.definitionFit: The digestive tract processes food, from mouth to gut.

clue.text: Plant cookware in stove so (10)

indicators.note: the cookware goes inside the stove

blocks.note: an Aga is a British range cooker

annotation.surface: An instruction to set pans in the oven, just so.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like the verb 'put'; it is the definition, a flower. An Aga is a heavy British range cooker.
annotation.definitionFit: Agapanthus, the African lily, is a garden plant with blue flower heads.

clue.text: Pottery line coming in handy (5)

indicators.note: the line comes into the other word

blocks.note: deft = handy, skilful; it opens round L

annotation.surface: A range of ceramics that proves useful.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pottery line' reads as a product range; the two words do separate jobs.
annotation.definitionFit: Delft is the blue and white glazed earthenware from the Dutch town of Delft.

clue.text: Latvian band including English characters (9)

indicators.note: the band includes E between its parts

annotation.surface: A Baltic pop group with some English members.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Characters' seems to mean people in a band; it is letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Characters here are letters of the alphabet, and the answer is letters written or painted collectively.

clue.text: Dingy tee I transformed with this? (3-6)

definitions.text: Dingy tee I transformed with this?

indicators.note: the letters are made over into a new form

annotation.surface: Someone brightens a dull T-shirt with a craft technique.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: tie-dyeing is how you would liven up a dingy T-shirt.
annotation.definitionFit: Tie-dyeing a drab tee would transform it into something colourful.

clue.text: Cooked mean melt with this? (8)

indicators.note: cooked letters are mixed and changed

annotation.surface: A question about which cheese makes a good melted sandwich.
annotation.walkthrough: A melt is a toasted sandwich with melted cheese, and Swiss Emmental is a classic one for it.
annotation.definitionFit: Emmental is a Swiss cheese that melts well, the thing you'd cook a melt with.

clue.text: Debacle minutes after agent for change nearly admits Conservative (9)

indicators.note: minutes come after the rest
nearly all of the word: drop the last letter
the shortened word lets C in

blocks.note: CATALYST without its last letter; it opens round C

annotation.surface: A political fiasco: a reformer nearly lets the Tories in and time runs out.
annotation.walkthrough: A catalyst is an agent that speeds up chemical change.
annotation.definitionFit: A cataclysm is a violent upheaval or disaster, a debacle.

clue.text: Artist dressed in light brown or dark brown (7)

indicators.note: the artist wears the brown, so it goes round him

blocks.note: camel = a light fawn colour; it opens round RA

annotation.surface: A painter chooses between two shades of brown clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface offers two browns; one is wordplay and one the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Named after burnt sugar, the colour is a deep golden brown, darker than camel.

clue.text: Give birth with assistance (5)

annotation.surface: A mother has her baby with a midwife's aid.
annotation.walkthrough: Whelp is used of dogs and other animals giving birth.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though used of dogs and other animals producing a litter rather than of people.

clue.text: Erode article, erode all round (7)

indicators.note: the second word goes all round the article

blocks.note: wear = erode, as water wears stone; it opens round THE

annotation.surface: A repetitive note: an item gets worn away on every side.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Erode' appears twice: the first is the definition, the second gives WEAR.
annotation.definitionFit: Rock weathers when wind and rain erode it.

clue.text: The giving of second award for sketch, perhaps (14)

blocks.note: an award handed over a second time: split the answer after RE
a sketch depicts something; 'perhaps' marks it as one example

annotation.surface: A prize is handed over twice for a drawing.
annotation.walkthrough: Split the answer as RE-PRESENTATION and it is a presentation made a second time. 'Perhaps' flags a sketch as just one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a sketch depicts its subject, as do a painting or a statue.

clue.text: American transporter used van failing to start (5)

indicators.note: each word fails to get its first letter

annotation.surface: A second-hand van that won't start.
annotation.walkthrough: Sedan is the American word for a saloon car. Both 'used' and 'van' lose their first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: Americans call a saloon car by this name, and a car transports people.

clue.text: Organic compound one is digging up? (5)

blocks.note: to mine is to dig up

annotation.surface: A question about which chemical a miner turns up.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'I mine': one digs up. The question mark flags that playful reading.
annotation.definitionFit: An imine is an organic compound containing a carbon-nitrogen double bond.

clue.text: Pizza shunned by California region (4)

indicators.note: the pizza has California shunned, so those letters leave

blocks.note: a calzone is a folded pizza

annotation.surface: Californians turn their noses up at pizza.
annotation.walkthrough: A calzone is a folded-over pizza; take CAL from it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an area marked off from those around it, as in a time zone.

clue.text: Hatred banning leader from platform (5)

indicators.note: ban the first letter from the word

annotation.surface: Public loathing keeps a political leader off the stage.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a leader no-platformed; the leader is only the P of podium.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually for the widespread loathing directed at a person, as in 'bear the odium'.

clue.text: Desire to cease cooking wheat in chef’s creation (5,4)

indicators.note: cooking turns raw ingredients into something new, so the letters are mixed up
the mixed letters go inside the dish

blocks.note: a dish is what a chef creates; it opens round EATHW

annotation.surface: A chef wants to stop putting wheat in the food.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Desire to cease' reads as wanting to stop cooking; it means a wish to cease living.
annotation.definitionFit: A death wish is a desire, conscious or not, for one's own death.

clue.text: Intend to stuff, say, great vegetable (8)

indicators.note: the plan is stuffed inside the other letters

blocks.note: Gt = great, as in Gt Britain; it opens round PLAN

annotation.surface: A cook means to fill a big vegetable.
annotation.walkthrough: Stuffing an aubergine is a real dish, so the surface is apt. Eggplant is the American name for the aubergine.
annotation.definitionFit: Eggplant is another name for the aubergine, a vegetable.

clue.text: Garment belonging to Glaswegian bachelor smells (6)

annotation.surface: A Glasgow single man's clothing stinks.
annotation.walkthrough: Breeks is the Scots word for trousers or breeches, hence the Glaswegian in the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Breeks are trousers in Scots dialect, a Glaswegian's garment.
